AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To describe the location, retrieval, frequency of surgery and complications associated with fishhook foreign bodies.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Retrospective evaluation of the medical records of cats and dogs admitted between 2010 and 2016 after fishhook ingestion.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: A total of 33 cases (2 cats and 31 dogs) were included. The most common locations were the proximal oesophagus [12/33 (36%)] and stomach [11/33 (33%)]. Endoscopic retrieval was successful in 27 of 33 cases (82%); oesophageal perforation was the only recorded complication, occurring in six of 33 (18%) cases. Surgery was performed in six cases (18%), and no early complications were recorded. The survival rate was 100%.

AbstractText.Label: CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE
AbstractText.content: The endoscopic removal of ingested fishhooks is highly successful. In the present study, survival to discharge was 100%, even in cases of oesophageal perforation or in cases requiring surgery.
